title: The people who never forget a face, with Josh Davis, PhD, and Kelly Desborough

sentences.en: Last year, we ran an episode about face blindness.
sentences.zh: 去年，我们播出一期关于面孔失认症的节目。

sentences.en: People who are face blind have trouble recognizing the faces of even their closest friends and family members.
sentences.zh: 面孔失认症患者甚至连认出自己最亲密的亲友的脸都有困难。

sentences.en: They're at one end of a spectrum of facial recognition ability.
sentences.zh: 他们处于面部识别能力光谱的一端。

sentences.en: And today, we're going to talk about the people at the other end of that bell curve, the super recognizers, or people who never forget a face.
sentences.zh: 而今天，我们要谈论的是处于这个钟形曲线另一端的人，也就是超级识别者，或者说那些过目不忘的人。

sentences.en: Scientists only began to study super recognizers a little over a decade ago.
sentences.zh: 科学家们在十多年前才开始研究超级识别者。

sentences.en: And since then, they've learned a great deal about this extraordinary ability.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，他们对这种非凡的能力有了深入的了解。

sentences.en: They've also begun to explore, together with police departments and other security organizations and businesses,
sentences.zh: 他们还开始与警察局以及其他安全机构和企业合作，

sentences.en: how super recognizers might contribute to police investigations and other security work.
sentences.zh: 探讨超级识别者如何为警方调查和其他安保工作做出贡献。

sentences.en: So how well can super recognizers remember faces?
sentences.zh: 那么，超级识别者的面部记忆力究竟有多强？

sentences.en: Can they really recognize a person whom they saw for only a few minutes many years ago?
sentences.zh: 他们真的能认出多年前只见过几分钟的人吗？

sentences.en: Are super recognizers as good as computer facial recognition algorithms?
sentences.zh: 超级识别者和计算机人脸识别算法一样厉害吗？

sentences.en: And can you train yourself to be a super recognizer, or at least improve your own facial recognition ability?
sentences.zh: 你能通过训练让自己成为超级识别者，或者至少提高自己的面部识别能力吗？

sentences.en: Or is this something you have to be born with?
sentences.zh: 还是说这是天生带来的？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: We have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天请到了两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: Our first is Dr. Josh Davis, a professor of applied psychology at the University of Greenwich in London.
sentences.zh: 第一位是乔什·戴维斯博士，他是伦敦格林威治大学的应用心理学教授。

sentences.en: Dr. Davis began his research career studying facial recognition ability and eyewitness identification.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯博士的研究生涯始于面部识别能力和目击者辨认的研究。

sentences.en: Since 2011, he has focused mainly on understanding super recognizers' exceptional abilities in this area.
sentences.zh: 自2011年以来，他主要致力于了解超级识别者在该领域的非凡能力。

sentences.en: He's developed screening tests to help better identify super recognizers, and he works with police departments and other organizations around the world
sentences.zh: 他开发了筛查测试以帮助更好地识别超级识别者，并与世界各地的警察局及其他机构合作，

sentences.en: to explore the ways in which super recognizers can contribute to security work.
sentences.zh: 探讨超级识别者能够以哪些方式为安保工作贡献力量。

sentences.en: Our second guest is Kelly Desbra.
sentences.zh: 我们的第二位嘉宾是凯莉·德斯布拉。

sentences.en: Ms. Desbra has always had an extraordinary ability to recognize and remember faces, but she didn't know that she was a super recognizer until about four years ago,
sentences.zh: 德斯布拉女士一直拥有识别和记忆面孔的非凡能力，但直到大约四年前，她并不知道自己是一名超级识别者，

sentences.en: when she took the online super recognizer screening test and received the highest score that researchers had ever seen.
sentences.zh: 当时她参加了在线超级识别者筛查测试，并获得了研究人员见过的最高分。

sentences.en: Today, she works for a company called Super Recognizers International, which trains and employs super recognizers to assist with everything from murder investigations
sentences.zh: 如今，她在一家名为“国际超级识别者”的公司工作，该公司培训和雇用超级识别者来协助处理各种事务，从谋杀案调查

sentences.en: to security at sporting events.
sentences.zh: 到体育赛事的安保。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining us today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢两位今天做客我们的节目。

sentences.en: Hi, Kim.
sentences.zh: 嗨，金。

sentences.en: Nice to see you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for inviting us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我们。

sentences.en: It's very exciting.
sentences.zh: 这太令人兴奋了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So we're going to go with first names here to just to keep it on a little informal basis.
sentences.zh: 那我们接下来就直呼其名，这样气氛能轻松一些。

sentences.en: So, Josh, let's start with you.
sentences.zh: 那么，乔什，我们先从你开始。

sentences.en: How do you identify and define a super recognizer?
sentences.zh: 你如何识别和定义超级识别者？

sentences.en: And how good does someone have to be at recognizing faces to qualify?
sentences.zh: 一个人要在面部识别上达到多高的水平才能符合条件？

sentences.en: On the whole, we've sort of set a rather arbitrary standard for super recognition that people should be able to be in the top 2% of the population,
sentences.zh: 总体而言，我们为超级识别设定了一个相当随意的标准，即人们应该能够进入人口的前2%，

sentences.en: achieving scores, should I say, on four primary criteria.
sentences.zh: 也就是在四个主要标准上达到相应的得分。

sentences.en: Short-term face memory, long-term face memory, simultaneous face matching, which is the art of passport officers checking identity documents that the person in front of them
sentences.zh: 短期面孔记忆、长期面孔记忆、同时面孔匹配——这就像护照官员核对身份证件，确认面前的人

sentences.en: is the person they say they are, and also spotting faces in a crowd.
sentences.zh: 就是他们所声称的那个人——以及在人群中发现面孔。

sentences.en: And we expect super recognizers to be in the top 2% on all four criteria.
sentences.zh: 我们期望超级识别者在这四个标准上都能进入前2%。

sentences.en: Kelly, did you always know this was something that you were very, very good at?
sentences.zh: 凯莉，你一直都知道自己在这方面非常非常厉害吗？

sentences.en: How did you first recognize that you had an extraordinary ability that everybody else didn't have?
sentences.zh: 你最初是如何发现自己拥有别人所没有的非凡能力的？

sentences.en: I had no idea.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道。

sentences.en: I had no idea that I was doing anything different to anybody else.
sentences.zh: 我根本不知道自己做的事情跟别人有什么不同。

sentences.en: So I imagined that people could recognize a person they hadn't seen for 30-odd years,
sentences.zh: 所以我以为所有人都能认出一个三十多年没见过、

sentences.en: that they'd only seen for a little while, or just noticed someone from a small part of their face.
sentences.zh: 当初也只见过一会儿的人，或者仅凭一小部分面部特征就能认出对方。

sentences.en: It's just, yeah, I thought everyone was doing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 就觉得，对啊，我以为大家都在做同样的事。

sentences.en: And I was reading a crime novel, and in that novel, the story tells of the detective who calls on the super recognizer unit at Scotland Yard to send them some help.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在读一本犯罪小说，书中讲到一个侦探向苏格兰场超级识别者小队寻求增援的故事。

sentences.en: So I googled the term super recognizer and found one of Josh's tests, did the test, and the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 于是我谷歌搜索了“超级识别者”这个词，找到了乔什的一项测试，做完之后，后面的事就顺理成章了。

sentences.en: So yes, I had no idea at all that I had this skill, and it turns out that it was something quite rare.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我完全不知道自己有这项技能，结果证明这是一种相当罕见的能力。

sentences.en: And do you have any examples from your daily lifetimes that you've recognized somebody from long ago or totally out of context?
sentences.zh: 你有没有日常生活中的例子，比如认出了很久以前的人，或者完全在出乎意料的场合认出某人？

sentences.en: I suppose there's two ways to explain it.
sentences.zh: 我想这可以从两种情况来解释。

sentences.en: One is somebody you know vaguely and somebody you don't know, and that's the really big one is the don't know person.
sentences.zh: 一种是你只有一面之缘的人，另一种是你完全不认识的人，而最厉害的是后面这种不认识的人。

sentences.en: But the example I would give is, I was in a local town at a parade, and I just, in a big crowd, I happened to look over my shoulder,
sentences.zh: 不过我要举的例子是，我在一个地方小镇的游行上，在茫茫人海中，我刚好回了一下头，

sentences.en: and I saw a girl stood a few people behind me, and I just glimpsed her for a split second.
sentences.zh: 我看到几个身位后方站着一个女孩，我只是匆匆瞥了她一眼。

sentences.en: And in that split second, I knew that that was Amber, who is the sister of a girl I went to kindergarten with 36 years prior.
sentences.zh: 就在那一瞬间，我知道那是安布尔，她是我36年前读幼儿园时一个朋友的姐姐。

sentences.en: And she wasn't even my friend, she was my friend's sister, who I think I saw a couple of times when I went round to play at my friend's house.
sentences.zh: 她甚至都不是我的朋友，她是我朋友的姐姐，我大概是在去朋友家玩的时候见过她几次。

sentences.en: But it was just that split second, and I worked out that it was 36 years since I would have last saw her.
sentences.zh: 但真的只是那一瞬间，我算了一下，距离我上次见到她已经过去36年了。

sentences.en: But again, at the time, I didn't know I was doing anything weird, I thought that was normal.
sentences.zh: 而且当时我并不知道自己在做什么奇怪的事，我以为这很正常。

sentences.en: And I would bound up to people and say, oh my goodness, I can't believe it, hi, how are you doing?
sentences.zh: 我会冲向别人说：“哦天哪，真不敢相信，嗨，你最近怎么样？”

sentences.en: And they would just look at me blankly as though I was a complete loon.
sentences.zh: 而他们只会茫然地看着我，仿佛我是个不折不扣的疯子。

sentences.en: And I would say, it's me, it's Kelly, and thinking, you know, they've clearly forgotten who I am, and I'm a forgettable type of person.
sentences.zh: 然后我会说：“是我啊，凯莉。”心里还想：他们显然把我给忘光了，我这人就是没什么存在感。

sentences.en: But I guess an example of the way a super recognizer works that illustrates it best is,
sentences.zh: 不过，如果要举一个最能说明超级识别者工作方式的例子，那就是：

sentences.en: I was given the image of a known predator that we were looking for at a sporting event.
sentences.zh: 有一次，我拿到了一张我们在某场体育赛事中搜寻的知名通缉犯的照片。

sentences.en: I looked at his face for maybe two or three seconds, and that imprinted it in my mind.
sentences.zh: 我看了他的脸也许两三秒钟，这个影像就印在了我的脑海里。

sentences.en: And I went into the crowd, and on that day, in that crowd, there were 42,000 people there, and I was able to find him and alert security to his presence there.
sentences.zh: 然后我走进人群，那天在那个场所有42,000人，我成功找到了他并向安保人员通报了他的出现。

sentences.en: So that's what a super recognizer can do.
sentences.zh: 这就是超级识别者能做到的事。

sentences.en: That just sounds miraculous.
sentences.zh: 这听起来简直像奇迹一样。

sentences.en: So, Josh, what do we know about how super recognizers are able to do this?
sentences.zh: 那么，乔什，对于超级识别者是如何做到这一点的，我们目前了解多少？

sentences.en: Do we have clues from brain imaging research or other studies?
sentences.zh: 我们能从脑成像研究或其他研究中找到什么线索吗？

sentences.en: We think, first of all, that's probably inherited.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们认为这很可能是遗传的。

sentences.en: At least face recognition ability seems to have a genetic component because if you run twin studies, as some researchers have done,
sentences.zh: 至少面部识别能力似乎具有基因成分，因为正如一些研究人员所做的那样，如果你进行双胞胎研究，

sentences.en: they find that identical twins tend to score far more similarly on face recognition tests than non-identical twins.
sentences.zh: 他们会发现同卵双胞胎在面部识别测试中的得分往往比异卵双胞胎要相似得多。

sentences.en: And as, of course, identical twins share 100% of their genes and non-identical twins share less of their genes,
sentences.zh: 当然，同卵双胞胎共享100%的基因，而异卵双胞胎共享的基因较少，

sentences.en: therefore, that seems to illustrate that we do have a genetic component.
sentences.zh: 因此，这似乎表明我们的确存在基因层面的影响。

sentences.en: And, in fact, we have done some parents and child testing, and we do find a correlation between a parent's ability and their child's ability.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们做了一些父母与孩子的测试，确实发现父母的能力与孩子的防守能力之间存在相关性。

sentences.en: And super recognizers score slightly higher than – sorry, the children of super recognizers tend to score higher than the children of controls.
sentences.zh: 而且超级识别者的得分略高——抱歉，超级识别者的孩子的得分往往比对照组的孩子更高。

sentences.en: So there's that genetic link.
sentences.zh: 所以存在这种基因层面的联系。

sentences.en: There does seem to be, from face recognition, something to do with your experiences as well.
sentences.zh: 从面部识别来看，这似乎也与你的经历有关。

sentences.en: And a very obvious example here is that most people are better at recognizing faces of their own ethnicity than of other faces,
sentences.zh: 这里有一个非常明显的例子：大多数人辨认自己种族的面孔比辨认其他种族的面孔更在行，

sentences.en: and it seems to happen with ages versus other ages as well.
sentences.zh: 不同年龄段之间似乎也是如此。

sentences.en: And we found that we had one super recognizer in a study in particular where we asked super recognizers to recognize baby faces.
sentences.zh: 在一项研究中，我们特别让超级识别者去辨认婴儿的面孔。

sentences.en: It's sort of the opposite to what Kelly is describing.
sentences.zh: 这有点像凯莉所描述的情况的反面。

sentences.en: And we found that adult super recognizers were better than controls at recognizing baby faces.
sentences.zh: 我们发现成年超级识别者在辨认婴儿面孔方面比对照组更强。

sentences.en: But in our sample, we coincidentally had a doctor who worked with babies all the time,
sentences.zh: 但在我们的样本中，我们碰巧有一位经常和婴儿打交道的医生，

sentences.en: and her scores were the only ones who were actually higher on the baby face test than the adult face test because she was used to faces.
sentences.zh: 她的得分是唯一一个在婴儿面孔测试中的表现实际上高于成年面孔测试的，因为她习惯了看婴儿的脸。

sentences.en: So there is something driving it with experience as well.
sentences.zh: 所以经历也在其中起到了一定的驱动作用。

sentences.en: And that seems to be the key factors.
sentences.zh: 这些似乎就是关键因素。

sentences.en: Kelly, you talked about recognizing somebody you hadn't seen since kindergarten, who clearly was now an adult.
sentences.zh: 凯莉，你刚才提到认出了一个自幼儿园毕业后再没见过、现在明显已经成年的人。

sentences.en: Is that common for you that you know somebody as a child and you see them 35 years later, and you know it's the same person, even though they've radically changed?
sentences.zh: 这对于你来说很常见吗：你认识一个人小时候的样子，35年后见到他们，尽管他们已经发生了翻天覆地的变化，但你还是知道这就是同一个人？

sentences.en: Yeah, it appears that time doesn't seem to really play a part in this.
sentences.zh: 是的，时间似乎在这个过程中并不起什么作用。

sentences.en: The facial features must stay similar enough for me to be able to recognize it.
sentences.zh: 面部特征一定保持了足够的相似性，我才能认出来。

sentences.en: But there can be 20, 30 more than that years apart, or they were a child, now they're an adult, and I can still tell them apart.
sentences.zh: 即便间隔20年、30年甚至更久，或者他们从小孩变成了成年人，我依然能把他们认出来。

sentences.en: So yeah, I can also recognize people who've drastically changed their appearance.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我也能认出外表发生剧烈变化的人。

sentences.en: So they might have facial hair, completely different hairstyle, different hair color.
sentences.zh: 他们可能留了胡子、换了完全不同的发型、染了不同的发色。

sentences.en: So it seems like the facial features will always remain imprinted, and I can pick them up.
sentences.zh: 因此，面部特征似乎永远会保留在记忆中，而我能把它们捕捉到。

sentences.en: Can I add to that?
sentences.zh: 我能补充一点吗？

sentences.en: I mean, the very first research on super recognizers used a before-they-were-famous teSt.
sentences.zh: 我是说，关于超级识别者的最早研究使用的是一项名为“成名之前”的测试。

sentences.en: This was by researchers in Harvard.
sentences.zh: 这是哈佛大学的研究人员做的。

sentences.en: And effectively, they showed famous people's photographs when they were children.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，他们展示了名人小时候的照片。

sentences.en: And the super recognizers are always far better at doing that type of teSt.
sentences.zh: 而超级识别者做这类测试总是要厉害得多。

sentences.en: We quite often use that as a demonstration when I'm giving talks to super recognizers or other people.
sentences.zh: 当我向超级识别者或其他听众做演讲时，我们经常用这个来做示范。

sentences.en: And you'll show, I don't know, a child image of, say, Britney Spears.
sentences.zh: 你会展示一张比如布兰妮·斯皮尔斯的儿童照片。

sentences.en: And the super recognizers, they've all got their hands up almost immediately, identifying Britney far quicker than everybody else.
sentences.zh: 然后超级识别者们几乎立刻就把手全举起来了，比其他任何人都要快得多地认出了布兰妮。

sentences.en: And, you know, people with average ability quite often just sit there going, no one can do this because it's impossible.
sentences.zh: 你知道，具备普通能力的人往往只是坐在那里觉得：没人能做到这一点，因为这根本不可能。

sentences.en: So something is happening.
sentences.zh: 所以这里面确实有些门道。

sentences.en: And we've used an unfamiliar type of project as well, where you'll show an adult face with three babies.
sentences.zh: 我们还使用过一种不熟悉的测试项目，即展示一张成人的脸和三个婴儿的照片。

sentences.en: And one of them is the adult.
sentences.zh: 其中一个婴儿就是那个成人。

sentences.en: And super recognizers tend to score higher on that one.
sentences.zh: 超级识别者在这项测试中的得分往往更高。

sentences.en: And yet they've never met the babies or the adults.
sentences.zh: 然而他们从未见过那些婴儿或成人。

sentences.en: So, Kelly, are you aware of what you're looking at when you look at a face?
sentences.zh: 那么，凯莉，当你看着一张脸时，你知道自己在看什么吗？

sentences.en: Do you focus on anything in specific or do you just get like a boom image of the whole face?
sentences.zh: 你会专注於某项特定内容，还是只是对整张脸有一个瞬间的整体印象？

sentences.en: Yeah, the latter.
sentences.zh: 是的，是后者。

sentences.en: I'm not looking at details.
sentences.zh: 我没有在看细节。

sentences.en: I just know it's a split second.
sentences.zh: 我只知道那是一瞬间的事。

sentences.en: It's a decision that just pops into my head.
sentences.zh: 这是一个直接蹦进我脑海里的决定。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I don't know how the science works.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我不知道其中的科学原理是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: And Josh might be able to elaborate.
sentences.zh: 乔什也许能详细说明。

sentences.en: Or I think they're still looking into it.
sentences.zh: 或者我想他们还在研究中。

sentences.en: Right, Josh?
sentences.zh: 对吧，乔什？

sentences.en: But I feel like I see the whole, I see the shape, I see a shape.
sentences.zh: 但我感觉我看到的是整体，我看到了轮廓，我看到了一个形状。

sentences.en: So I can get people from the backs of their heads too.
sentences.zh: 所以我从人们的后脑勺也能认出他们。

sentences.en: So that tells me that I'm seeing a shape of someone rather than the facial features.
sentences.zh: 这说明我看到的是某人的轮廓，而不是面部特征。

sentences.en: And also I can tell them from just a small part of their face.
sentences.zh: 而且我仅凭他们脸部的一小部分就能认出他们。

sentences.en: Or if they're wearing a mask, I can tell them from their eyes.
sentences.zh: 或者如果他们戴着口罩，我能从他们的眼睛认出来。

sentences.en: And so the masks haven't caused a problem in identifying people.
sentences.zh: 所以口罩并没有给辨认人员造成困扰。

sentences.en: So throughout the pandemic, it hasn't impaired your ability to basically do your job, right?
sentences.zh: 所以在整个疫情期间，这并没有削弱你基本的工作能力，对吧？

sentences.en: No, no, it's not as easy.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有，当然没那么容易。

sentences.en: Don't get me wrong.
sentences.zh: 别误会我的意思。

sentences.en: But, you know, there's still that instantaneous recognition if you do see the person you're looking for.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，如果你真的看到了你要找的人，仍然会有那种瞬间的识别感。

sentences.en: I could add to that that we have done research.
sentences.zh: 我可以补充一点，我们做过相关研究。

sentences.en: We found super recognisers were better than controls at recognising faces with face masks on, whether they were familiar with them or unfamiliar.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，无论是熟悉的面孔还是陌生的面孔，超级识别者在辨认戴口罩的面孔时都比对照组更强。

sentences.en: And something else that Kelly said that strikes me was that we have done research using EEG as well, measuring brain activity.
sentences.zh: 凯莉刚才说的另一件事也让我印象深刻，那就是我们也使用脑电图（EEG）测量大脑活动进行了研究。

sentences.en: And we also found that super recognisers seem to have a greater spike of activity very early in face processing when they saw a face that was familiar to them in comparison to controls.
sentences.zh: 我们还发现，与对照组相比，当超级识别者看到熟悉的面孔时，他们在面部处理的极早期似乎会出现更大的活动峰值。

sentences.en: And that might link to what Kelly said about sort of instantaneously being able to recognise as someone familiar to them as well.
sentences.zh: 这可能与凯莉所说的能够瞬间认出熟悉之人的情况有关。

sentences.en: But that does need some replication.
sentences.zh: 不过这还需要进一步的重复验证。

sentences.en: It was published in Cortex, which is quite a nice journal to get published in.
sentences.zh: 这项研究发表在《Cortex》上，这是一本非常不错的学术期刊。

sentences.en: So, you know which part of the brain or parts of the brain are involved in recognition at this point, Josh?
sentences.zh: 那么，乔什，到目前为止，你知道大脑的哪个部分或哪些部分参与了识别过程吗？

sentences.en: That particular research was EEG, which measures activity.
sentences.zh: 那项特定的研究使用的是脑电图，它测量的是活动情况。

sentences.en: And if you like, it's not very good at geographically mapping the areas in the brain that is active at the time.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，它不太擅长在地理空间上定位当时活跃的大脑区域。

sentences.en: But other people have done fMRI studies, which is far more accurate at measuring the brain.
sentences.zh: 但其他人做过功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）研究，这在测量大脑方面要精准得多。

sentences.en: And there's an area that seems to be associated with face recognition called the fusiform gyrus.
sentences.zh: 有一个区域似乎与面部识别有关，叫做梭状回。

sentences.en: And when that area gets damaged, for instance, people often develop prosopagnosia as you introduce the topic and become face blind.
sentences.zh: 当这个区域受损时，例如，正如你开场提到的那样，人们经常会患上脸盲症，变得无法认出面孔。

sentences.en: So, there is a lot of evidence from fMRI as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，来自fMRI的证据也很多。

sentences.en: It's more active when people are viewing faces.
sentences.zh: 当人们观看面孔时，这个区域会更加活跃。

sentences.en: So, Kelly, I have to ask you a question on behalf of our producer, Lee Weinerman, who is the mother of identical twins.
sentences.zh: 凯莉，我必须代表我们的制片人李·韦纳曼向你提个问题，她是同卵双胞胎的母亲。

sentences.en: Do identical twins look different to you all the time?
sentences.zh: 对你来说，同卵双胞胎看起来总是不同的吗？

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全不同。

sentences.en: Yeah, I have identical twins in my family and I spent a lot of time with them when they were younger.
sentences.zh: 是的，我家里有同卵双胞胎，在他们小的时候，我花了很多时间跟他们在一起。

sentences.en: So, when they were toddlers and I saw them as two completely separate faces.
sentences.zh: 所以，当他们还是幼儿时，我就把他们看作两个完全独立的面孔。

sentences.en: And again, I wish I'd have known why I was seeing that at the time.
sentences.zh: 而且话说回来，我希望当时能知道为什么自己会有那种视觉体验。

sentences.en: But no, they just, again, in a glimpse or a side view, I would know which one was Kirsty and which one was Lacey.
sentences.zh: 但不用，他们只要——再次强调，哪怕只是惊鸿一瞥或侧面，我也能分清哪个是柯丝蒂，哪个是莱西。

sentences.en: And yeah, although I fully appreciate how similar they look, obviously, but I can completely tell them apart.
sentences.zh: 而且是的，尽管我完全能看出他们长得有多像，但我确实能把他们完全区分开。

sentences.en: They're just, the differences are glaringly obvious to me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，他们之间的区别实在是太明显了。

sentences.en: Well, let me ask you both this one.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我问你们俩一个问题。

sentences.en: Do super recognisers have better than average memory in any other areas of life?
sentences.zh: 超级辨脸者在生活中的其他领域是否拥有高于平均水平的记忆力？

sentences.en: Well, I can answer that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我来回答这个问题。

sentences.en: We have used object memory tests and some other sort of visual processing tests.
sentences.zh: 我们使用过物体记忆测试和其他一些视觉处理测试。

sentences.en: And they tend to be slightly better than controls at these other tests, suggesting that they do have superior, you know, memory for visual things in general.
sentences.zh: 在这些其他测试中，他们的表现往往比对照组略好一些，这表明他们对一般视觉事物的记忆确实更胜一筹。

sentences.en: But actually, the differences between controls and super recognisers are far greater when it comes to faces.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，当涉及面孔时，对照组和超级辨脸者之间的差距要大得多。

sentences.en: And perhaps we found voices as well.
sentences.zh: 也许我们在声音方面也发现了这一点。

sentences.en: We've done some recent research, finding that they tend to be slightly better at voices, which might suggest that it's something about human identification, human recognition,
sentences.zh: 我们最近做了一些研究，发现他们在辨别声音方面往往也略胜一筹，这或许表明这与人类的身份识别和人类识别有关，

sentences.en: rather than purely face recognition.
sentences.zh: 而不仅仅是单纯的面部识别。

sentences.en: Kelly's always described her ability to recognise people by other things from the back of the head sometimes.
sentences.zh: 凯莉总是描述她通过其他特征来识别人的能力，有时甚至通过后脑勺。

sentences.en: So it's not just about the face.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅关乎面部。

sentences.en: And you just mentioned voice recognition as well.
sentences.zh: 你刚才也提到了声音识别。

sentences.en: Is that another burgeoning area of research right now that people can just tell who someone is based on hearing their voice?
sentences.zh: 这是否是目前另一个蓬勃发展的研究领域，即人们仅凭听到声音就能分辨出某人是谁？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I have a PhD student, Ryan Jenkins, who's been researching voice recognition.
sentences.zh: 我有一个博士生瑞安·詹金斯，他一直在研究声音识别。

sentences.en: We find that people with super recognition ability for faces tend to be better at voices as well.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在面部识别方面具有超强能力的人，在声音识别方面往往也更强。

sentences.en: But it's not 100% by any means.
sentences.zh: 但这绝不是百分之百的。

sentences.en: It's a small proportion.
sentences.zh: 这只占很小的一部分。

sentences.en: And so that research is ongoing.
sentences.zh: 所以这项研究仍在进行中。

sentences.en: One of the things is developing tests to actually measure this ability is always a bit harder than it perhaps you imagine when you start down this PhD progress.
sentences.zh: 其中一件事是，开发实际测量这种能力的测试，总是比你在开始攻读博士学位时想象的要困难一些。

sentences.en: So a few minutes ago, Josh mentioned that there's a genetic component to this.
sentences.zh: 所以几分钟前，乔希提到这其中有基因的成分。

sentences.en: So, Kelly, are there other people in your family who have this ability?
sentences.zh: 那么，凯莉，你家里还有其他人拥有这种能力吗？

sentences.en: I think that my mum, my mother might have it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我妈妈，我母亲可能也有。

sentences.en: So she's pulled some stunts that I think that would suggest that she found a phone, an iPhone on the floor in a public garden.
sentences.zh: 她曾做过一些让我觉得能说明问题的事，比如她在公共花园的地上捡到了一部 iPhone。

sentences.en: And she picked it up and it was somebody was calling it and it showed the face of the person calling.
sentences.zh: 她把它捡起来，当时有人在打电话，屏幕上显示着来电者的头像。

sentences.en: And she knew she'd just walked past that person.
sentences.zh: 而她知道自己刚刚从那个人身边走过。

sentences.en: So she took it back to them.
sentences.zh: 于是她把手机送还给了失主。

sentences.en: So I said, mum, I think maybe something's going on here.
sentences.zh: 所以我对她说，妈，我觉得你身上可能有点什么特异功能。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I would say she's a high she's got a high potential there.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，可以说她在这方面很有潜力。

sentences.en: So she hasn't taken the test?
sentences.zh: 那她没有做过测试吗？

sentences.en: She hasn't.
sentences.zh: 她还没做过。

sentences.en: She's probably too scared to fail.
sentences.zh: 她可能太害怕失败了。

sentences.en: I'm going to encourage her.
sentences.zh: 我打算鼓励她去测一下。

sentences.en: So is facial recognition ability something you can train yourself to do or even to just get better at?
sentences.zh: 那么面部识别能力是可以通过训练获得的，甚至只是为了有所提高吗？

sentences.en: Some researchers have tried to teach people to be better at face recognition, in particular in perhaps the sort of identity verification role, such as passport officers,
sentences.zh: 一些研究人员试图教导人们提高面部识别能力，特别是在身份核查的角色中，比如护照查验官员，

sentences.en: because that's so important.
sentences.zh: 因为这太重要了。

sentences.en: So perhaps you can improve slightly the ability to perhaps do a face matching task by asking people to focus on features or other aspects of the face.
sentences.zh: 所以，通过要求人们专注于面部的特征或其他方面，或许可以稍微提高进行面部匹配任务的能力。

sentences.en: It doesn't seem to improve face recognition in general, this type of training scheme.
sentences.zh: 这种训练计划似乎并不能总体上提高面部识别能力。

sentences.en: So I'm afraid your ability seems to peak at about 30 years of age, keeps improving beyond the teenage years.
sentences.zh: 所以恐怕你的这项能力在30岁左右就会达到顶峰，它在青少年时期之后会不断提高。

sentences.en: But then there's a long, unfortunate, slow decline from that point on.
sentences.zh: 但从那以后，就会开始一个漫长、不幸且缓慢的衰退过程。

sentences.en: Well, then perhaps it's lucky, Kelly, that you also are a professional photographer, which is also a visual field.
sentences.zh: 那么，凯莉，你同时还是一名专业摄影师，这同样也是一个视觉领域，这或许很幸运。

sentences.en: Do you feel that it's linked in any way to your super recognizing ability?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这与你的超级辨脸能力有什么联系吗？

sentences.en: And do you only take portraits?
sentences.zh: 而且你只拍人像吗？

sentences.en: No, I do all sorts of commercial photography.
sentences.zh: 不，我拍各种各样的商业摄影。

sentences.en: So I don't think it's linked, to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 所以说实话，我觉得这没有什么联系。

sentences.en: There's all sorts of different people from different walks of life, different skills that are super recognizers.
sentences.zh: 超级辨脸者来自各行各业，拥有各种不同的技能。

sentences.en: And I can't see a pattern there.
sentences.zh: 我看不出有什么规律可言。

sentences.en: I put a lot of attention to detail in my work and I am meticulous.
sentences.zh: 我在工作中投入了大量的对细节的关注，而且我一丝不苟。

sentences.en: And that helps with my job.
sentences.zh: 这确实对我的工作有帮助。

sentences.en: But I don't see a link.
sentences.zh: 但我看不出它们之间有什么联系。

sentences.en: I don't see a link there.
sentences.zh: 我看不出有什么联系。

sentences.en: Well, speaking of jobs, your other job, as I mentioned in the intro, was that you work for Super Recognizers International, doing investigative and security identification work.
sentences.zh: 说到工作，正如我在开场白中提到的，你的另一份工作是为国际超级辨脸组织工作，从事调查和安全识别工作。

sentences.en: What kind of organizations do you work with and what do you do for them on an average day?
sentences.zh: 你与什么样的组织合作？在平常的一天里，你为他们做什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, I work for law enforcement agencies, police departments, security, private security companies.
sentences.zh: 是的，我为执法机构、警察局、安全公司以及私人保安公司工作。

sentences.en: And we do all sorts of things from, as you mentioned, murder investigations, assault investigations through to live events where we're on foot doing covert operations,
sentences.zh: 我们做各种各样的事情，正如你所提到的，从谋杀案调查、攻击案调查，一直到我们在现场徒步进行秘密行动的现场活动，

sentences.en: looking for people in crowds.
sentences.zh: 在人群中寻找目标人物。

sentences.en: So there's a variety of ways in which we can apply the skill.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们可以通过多种方式应用这项技能。

sentences.en: We can produce facial comparison reports for people who are trying to prove the identity of somebody.
sentences.zh: 我们可以为那些试图证明某人身份的人制作面部比对报告。

sentences.en: So it's very varied.
sentences.zh: 所以工作内容非常多样化。

sentences.en: And I'm also working on quite quick, moving investigations, such as missing people, trafficked and exploited children.
sentences.zh: 我也在参与一些节奏相当快的调查，例如失踪人口、被拐卖和受虐待的儿童。

sentences.en: I work for the NCPTF, which is the National Child Protection Task Force over in America there, who do an amazing job investigating missing children and rescuing them.
sentences.zh: 我为美国国家儿童保护工作组（NCPTF）工作，他们在调查失踪儿童和营救儿童方面做着了不起的工作。

sentences.en: They're amazing as a global force that are volunteering together to help.
sentences.zh: 作为一个自愿联合起来提供帮助的全球力量，他们太棒了。

sentences.en: And I'm one of their, what they like to call mutants.
sentences.zh: 我是他们喜欢称之为“变种人”的其中一员。

sentences.en: They have a team of all sorts of different skills.
sentences.zh: 他们的团队拥有各种各样不同的技能。

sentences.en: And I'm proud to say I'm one of their mutants.
sentences.zh: 我很自豪地说我是他们的变种人之一。

sentences.en: So, yeah, that's the sort of thing we're doing.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这就是我们正在做的事情。

sentences.en: And have you found missing children yourself?
sentences.zh: 你自己找到过失踪儿童吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 找到过。

sentences.en: That must be very, very satisfying.
sentences.zh: 那一定非常非常有成就感。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I'm able to be given some faces of children that we know are being exploited.
sentences.zh: 我能够获得一些我们知道正受到虐待的儿童的面孔照片。

sentences.en: We have the predator as well.
sentences.zh: 我们也能接触到虐童惯犯。

sentences.en: I had a case where we had a predator and two children linked together.
sentences.zh: 我曾遇到这样一个案子，我们锁定了虐童犯和两个受害儿童。

sentences.en: I was able to find links to them online and we picked them up around six hours after I identified them.
sentences.zh: 我在网上找到了与他们相关的线索，并在我认出他们大约六个小时后，我们就找到了他们。

sentences.en: So my leads will be given to the police department who are investigating that.
sentences.zh: 所以我的线索会被提供给负责调查的警察局。

sentences.en: So, obviously, I don't just say it's them, go get them.
sentences.zh: 很显然，我不会只是说“就是他们，去抓他们”。

sentences.en: They will have to do a thorough investigation.
sentences.zh: 他们必须进行彻底的调查。

sentences.en: So I'm just the lead.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是提供线索。

sentences.en: And then it saves them days, weeks, months of searching and trawling.
sentences.zh: 这为他们节省了数天、数周甚至数月的搜寻和大海捞针的时间。

sentences.en: I can get them results really quickly.
sentences.zh: 我可以非常迅速地为他们提供结果。

sentences.en: Then they can follow those leads.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就可以顺藤摸瓜。

sentences.en: And in that case, it's six hours before they were, the kids were rescued and the predator was arrested.
sentences.zh: 在那起案件中，从我发现线索到孩子们被解救、虐童犯被捕，仅仅过去了六个小时。

sentences.en: So, yeah, we're getting some brilliant results.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们取得了非常棒的成果。

sentences.en: We've had some great results in murder investigations, too,
sentences.zh: 我们在谋杀案调查中也取得了一些极好的成果，

sentences.en: where my evidence has helped to narrow down timelines for the police and improve premeditation so I can create a nice package of evidence for the prosecution.
sentences.zh: 我的证据帮助警方缩小了时间范围，并证实了蓄意谋杀，因此我能为控方整理出一套极佳的证据包。

sentences.en: In recent years, we've heard a lot about artificial intelligence, facial identification algorithms, and how they're being used in everything from social media to policing.
sentences.zh: 近年来，我们听到了很多关于人工智能、面部识别算法的讨论，以及它们如何被应用到从社交媒体到警务工作的方方面面。

sentences.en: Well, there are obviously some ethical and legal questions around this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，围绕这一点显然存在一些伦理和法律问题。

sentences.en: But just as a purely practical question, are super recognizers as good as AI algorithms or are they better?
sentences.zh: 但仅从纯粹的实用角度来看，超级辨脸者的表现和 AI 算法一样好吗，还是说他们更好？

sentences.en: So the last big piece of research really on this was done in the United States.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，真正的大型研究实际上是在美国进行的。

sentences.en: And they recruited super recognizers, controls, also forensic facial analysts.
sentences.zh: 他们招募了超级辨脸者、对照组，还有法医面部鉴定专家。

sentences.en: And the best algorithms at the time, as identified by the National Institute of Science and Technology in the USA.
sentences.zh: 以及当时由美国国家标准与技术研究院认定的最佳算法。

sentences.en: And they found that the super recognizers were operating at the same level as the best algorithms and far better than controls.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，超级辨脸者的表现与最佳算法处于同一水平，并且远优于对照组。

sentences.en: But what they also found, which I think is really key here, is that actually if you combined the decision-making of a super recognizer with an algorithm, accuracy was even higher.
sentences.zh: 但他们还发现了一点，我认为这才是真正的关键所在，那就是如果你将超级辨脸者的决策与算法结合起来，准确率甚至会更高。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons is because algorithms make mistakes that a human would never make.
sentences.zh: 原因之一是算法会犯人类永远不会犯的错误。

sentences.en: And humans make mistakes that an algorithm probably wouldn't make.
sentences.zh: 而人类也会犯算法可能不会犯的错误。

sentences.en: So, therefore, you're removing those errors that are probably unique to both and getting better outcomes.
sentences.zh: 因此，你可以消除那些各自独有的错误，从而获得更好的结果。

sentences.en: Does AI have the ability that Kelly described, which is she can tell people from seeing the backs of their heads?
sentences.zh: 人工智能具备凯莉所描述的那种能力吗？即通过看别人的后脑勺就能认出人。

sentences.en: Almost certainly not.
sentences.zh: 几乎可以肯定没有。

sentences.en: I don't think because AI has to be trained with images for it to be able to perform these tasks.
sentences.zh: 我认为不能，因为人工智能必须通过图像进行训练才能执行这些任务。

sentences.en: And I don't think there are any databases of faces from the back of the head to train AI.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为没有任何后脑勺的数据库来训练人工智能。

sentences.en: So that's how it works.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的工作原理。

sentences.en: So you have to sort of throw into the mix hundreds, if not thousands, of faces for AI to be most effective, a bit like humans.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了让人工智能发挥最大效用，你必须把成百上千张面孔投入其中进行混合训练，这有点像人类。

sentences.en: And if you haven't got those images, then humans are going to beat AI every single time.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有这些图像，那么人类每一次都会战胜人工智能。

sentences.en: And we can also deal with really low-quality images, you know, really pixelated images aren't going to deter us.
sentences.zh: 而且我们还能处理画质极低的图像，你知道的，极其模糊像素化的图像不会难倒我们。

sentences.en: And also, you know, like I said, masks, facial hair, bits and pieces that might throw an algorithm off.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，正如我所说，面具、面部毛发以及其他可能难倒算法的零碎东西，

sentences.en: We kind of override those.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上都能克服。

sentences.en: So I think I am a great advocate of facial recognition software and I enjoy working with it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我是面部识别软件的坚定支持者，我也很乐意与它合作。

sentences.en: And I get some of my best results when I team up with guys that use facial recognition software.
sentences.zh: 当我与使用面部识别软件的同行组队时，我总能取得最好的成果。

sentences.en: So I think putting the two of us together makes a superpower.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得把我们两个结合起来就成了一种超能力。

sentences.en: So is it your view that people who check passports, say, in customs, should we be testing people for their facial recognition ability before they get jobs like this?
sentences.zh: 那么在你看，例如在海关检查护照的人员，我们在他们获得这类工作之前，是否应该测试他们的面部识别能力？

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对应该。

sentences.en: And they do in some countries.
sentences.zh: 有些国家已经在这样做了。

sentences.en: You would never want someone with face blindness, prosopagnosia, being a passport officer because they just could not do the job.
sentences.zh: 你绝对不会想让患有面孔失认症（即脸盲症）的人去当护照查验官，因为他们根本无法胜任这项工作。

sentences.en: I'm not necessarily sure that you need super recognisers for that job.
sentences.zh: 我倒不一定确信该工作非得需要超级辨脸者不可。

sentences.en: But what you want is people who have above average abilities in those sorts of roles because they're far more likely to make a correct identification.
sentences.zh: 但你需要的是在这些岗位上拥有高于平均水平能力的人，因为他们更有可能做出正确的识别。

sentences.en: But they're also far more likely not to make a wrong identification than people with average or lower ability.
sentences.zh: 而且与能力平平或较低的人相比，他们也更不可能做出错误的识别。

sentences.en: That's key as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是关键所在。

sentences.en: Kelly, does the company that you work for advocate for this?
sentences.zh: 凯莉，你所在的机构是否倡导这一点？

sentences.en: I mean, do you consult to, you know, operations that maybe could use some sort of a test for their employees?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你们是否会为那些可能需要对员工进行某种测试的机构提供咨询？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: We team up with lots of different companies to assiSt.
sentences.zh: 我们与许多不同的公司合作以提供协助。

sentences.en: We work for a company that do assess passport photographs and ID photos.
sentences.zh: 我们为一家评估护照照片和身份证照片的公司工作。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's definitely something we can apply and help with.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这绝对是我们能够应用和提供帮助的领域。

sentences.en: And we do identify super recognisers through the testing.
sentences.zh: 我们确实通过测试来识别超级辨脸者。

sentences.en: And then we put them through our own training courses, which will teach them all about the law surrounding image use.
sentences.zh: 然后我们让他们接受我们自己的培训课程，这些课程将向他们传授有关图像使用法律的所有知识。

sentences.en: It will enhance their skills with behavioural analysis as well if we're actually out and about.
sentences.zh: 如果我们实际在户外执勤，它还将提高他们在行为分析方面的技能。

sentences.en: So, we can enhance skills around super recognition too to make a really rounded super recognisers that's able to go out into the world and use their skill for good.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们也可以提升围绕超级辨脸的技能，从而培养出真正全面的超级辨脸者，让他们能够走向世界，将自己的技能用于正道。

sentences.en: So, some of our listeners might not be aware that in your country, and you're both in England, that there are closed circuit TVs pretty much everywhere, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，我们的一些听众可能不知道，在你们国家——你们都在英国——几乎到处都有闭路电视，对吧？

sentences.en: You folks are on camera all the time.
sentences.zh: 你们这些人时时刻刻都在镜头监视之下。

sentences.en: It's a little different from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这与美国有点不同，

sentences.en: where, you know, we're very sort of hinky about that concept.
sentences.zh: 在美国，你知道的，我们对这种概念非常敏感别扭。

sentences.en: Are there ethical issues surrounding what it is that you do, for example, trying to find criminals?
sentences.zh: 你们所做的事情（比如试图寻找罪犯）是否存在伦理问题？

sentences.en: I mean, do people in England feel like their privacy has been invaded?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，英国人会觉得自己隐私被侵犯了吗？

sentences.en: So, they do worry about privacy in terms of computerised face recognition systems, definitely.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们在计算机化面部识别系统方面确实会担心隐私问题，肯定的。

sentences.en: But I don't think anybody worries about super recognisers because, if you like, they epitomise what an old-fashioned police officer should be able to do.
sentences.zh: 但我认为没有人会担心超级辨脸者，因为如果你愿意的话，他们就是老式警察应该具备的能力的缩影。

sentences.en: They know all the criminals.
sentences.zh: 他们认识所有的罪犯。

sentences.en: You see it on cop shows.
sentences.zh: 你在警匪片里也能看到。

sentences.en: There's nothing strange about super recognisers within policing identifying criminals and people like that.
sentences.zh: 在警务工作中，通过超级辨脸来识别罪犯和类似人员并不是什么稀奇事。

sentences.en: Everyone expects it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都习以为常。

sentences.en: It's the algorithms they are more suspicious of, definitely.
sentences.zh: 他们更怀疑的绝对是那些算法。

sentences.en: And it's a way of life for us being on camera.
sentences.zh: 活在镜头下对我们来说已经是生活方式的一部分。

sentences.en: I would far rather that my whole country was covered in cameras.
sentences.zh: 我宁愿我的整个国家都布满摄像头。

sentences.en: And if something happens to me or one of my loved ones, that it's going to get picked up and we're going to have some evidence to work from.
sentences.zh: 这样如果我和我爱的人身上发生了什么事，它会被拍下来，我们就会有证据可以着手调查。

sentences.en: The number of cases that are solved through surveillance footage and, you know, come to a conclusion much quicker and more accurately because of that.
sentences.zh: 通过监控录像破获的案件数量繁多，而且正因为如此，案件得以更迅速、更准确地告破。

sentences.en: I'm a strong believer that we should stick cameras everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我坚信我们应该到处安装摄像头。

sentences.en: And I certainly have them all over my house.
sentences.zh: 而且我的房子里确实到处都是。

sentences.en: I don't.
sentences.zh: 我可没有。

sentences.en: For me personally, I'm protective of my privacy, but I do agree that in some areas you do want cameras.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我很注重保护隐私，但我确实同意在某些区域需要摄像头。

sentences.en: You want them in town centres and airports and places like that, train stations, travel centres, and they should be scrutinised properly.
sentences.zh: 你希望在市中心、机场以及类似的地方、火车站、交通枢纽看到它们，而且它们应该受到适当的审查。

sentences.en: So my understanding is that the cameras were installed because there was the thinking among law enforcement that they would be a deterrent.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，安装摄像头是因为执法部门认为它们能起到威慑作用。

sentences.en: But it seems that they're not, that a lot of people will just blithely go about committing crimes because they figure there are tens and thousands and millions of these images.
sentences.zh: 但事实似乎并非如此，很多人只是无忧无虑地去犯罪，因为他们觉得有成千上万、数以百万计的影像。

sentences.en: No one's ever going to find me.
sentences.zh: 没人能找到我。

sentences.en: Do you feel that the public, at least in the UK, is aware of the fact that you have been able to crack a lot of cases?
sentences.zh: 你觉得公众，至少在英国，是否意识到你已经成功破获了很多案件？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's been very important.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这非常重要。

sentences.en: The super recognisers successes that have been in the media.
sentences.zh: 超级面孔识别者的成功已经在媒体上得到了报道。

sentences.en: In fact, my PhD was on the way that faces are used in court for identification purposes.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我的博士论文就是关于法庭上如何使用面孔进行身份识别的。

sentences.en: And at that time, they weren't at all.
sentences.zh: 而在那个时候，他们根本不用这个。

sentences.en: There was a lot of cameras around and nobody was ever really looking at them.
sentences.zh: 当时有很多摄像头，但从来没有人真正去看它们。

sentences.en: It's only later that they started properly scrutinising the images, making sure that they actually try and identify people committing crimes on camera.
sentences.zh: 直到后来，他们才开始认真审查这些图像，确保他们真正尝试识别在摄像头前犯罪的人。

sentences.en: And that breeds success.
sentences.zh: 这就带来了成功。

sentences.en: More success, you get more criminals identified.
sentences.zh: 更多的成功，你就能识别出更多的罪犯。

sentences.en: And so much so that, you know, my work has transferred to other countries around the world.
sentences.zh: 以至于你知道我的工作已经扩展到了世界上的其他国家。

sentences.en: Especially at the moment, we're identifying a lot of super recognisers within German police forces, super recognisers in India, working in identity verification,
sentences.zh: 特别是目前，我们在德国警察部队中识别出了很多超级面孔识别者，在印度的超级面孔识别者正从事身份验证工作，

sentences.en: creating lots of jobs there for people, working in sort of roles, checking identity documents for the government and other organisations.
sentences.zh: 为当地人们创造了大量的工作岗位，从事为政府和其他组织检查身份证件等工作。

sentences.en: We're not really working in America, in the USA, as of yet.
sentences.zh: 我们目前还没有真正在美国开展工作。

sentences.en: But who knows?
sentences.zh: 但谁知道呢？

sentences.en: I'm on my way.
sentences.zh: 我在路上了。

sentences.en: I'm coming to get you.
sentences.zh: 我来抓你们了。

sentences.en: So, Kelly, I mean, it sounds like you really appreciate this ability that you have.
sentences.zh: 那么，凯莉，我的意思是，听起来你真的很感激自己拥有的这项能力。

sentences.en: But I'm wondering if you ever feel that there are drawbacks.
sentences.zh: 但我在想，你是否曾觉得这也有缺点？

sentences.en: I mean, do people try to fool you?
sentences.zh: 我是说，有人试图愚弄你吗？

sentences.en: I don't see any drawbacks.
sentences.zh: 我没觉得有什么缺点。

sentences.en: I think it's a relief now I know I'm not being stalked constantly.
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在很解脱，因为我知道自己没有遭到不间断的跟踪。

sentences.en: Because, of course, if you're walking around a shopping mall and you see the same person over and over again, you start to think, I'm being followed by this person.
sentences.zh: 因为当然了，如果你在购物中心走来走去，看到同一个人一遍又一遍地出现，你就会开始觉得，我被这个人跟踪了。

sentences.en: But essentially what's happening is I'm just recognising the same person in the same shopping mall with me.
sentences.zh: 但实际上发生的情况是，我只是在同一个购物中心里认出了同一个人。

sentences.en: There's nothing worse than that.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比这更糟糕的了。

sentences.en: So there aren't really any drawbacks, to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 所以说实话，真的没什么缺点。

sentences.en: It's very useful.
sentences.zh: 这非常有用。

sentences.en: It's a bit annoying for people who are around me when I keep telling them that that's the guy in the film 20 years ago that was an extra in Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade.
sentences.zh: 对于我身边的人来说有点烦人，因为我总是告诉他们，那个人就是20世纪电影里在《夺宝奇兵3》里跑龙套的家伙。

sentences.en: But no, I embrace the skill.
sentences.zh: 但我不，我欣然接受这项技能。

sentences.en: I'm so delighted that I can use it for good, that I'm seeing results that are meaning something to families who have lost somebody or who are fighting for justice.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我能用它来做善事，我看到的结果对那些失去亲人或为正义而战的家庭来说意义重大。

sentences.en: So it's just an honour that I'm able to translate this skill into something useful for society.
sentences.zh: 所以，能把这项技能转化为对社会有用的东西，我感到非常荣幸。

sentences.en: So, Josh, last question.
sentences.zh: 那么，乔什，最后一个问题。

sentences.en: Where is the research going next?
sentences.zh: 这项研究接下来将走向何方？

sentences.en: Well, that's a big question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个宏大的问题。

sentences.en: We would like to do some more brain scanning research to try and understand exactly what's going on in super recognisers' brains.
sentences.zh: 我们希望做更多的大脑扫描研究，试图弄清楚超级面孔识别者的大脑中到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And then perhaps from that, we can understand how to better apply their skills in different workforces for whatever reason.
sentences.zh: 然后也许由此我们可以了解如何出于各种原因更好地将他们的技能应用到不同的工作岗位中。

sentences.en: Because we don't really know where we might end up going in the future for the best use of super recognisers.
sentences.zh: 因为我们真的不知道未来我们会走向何方，才能最好地利用超级面孔识别者。

sentences.en: I'm probably more of an applied psychologist than a theoretical psychologist, more interested in seeing, you know, the practical aspects work like Kelly does.
sentences.zh: 我可能更像是一个应用心理学家，而不是理论心理学家，我更热衷于看到像凯莉那样实际层面的成果发挥作用。

sentences.en: How else can we use Kelly's skills to, you know, help society in general?
sentences.zh: 我们还能如何利用凯莉的技能来帮助整个社会呢？

sentences.en: Are there places that we're missing the use of super recognition, Kelly?
sentences.zh: 凯莉，有没有哪些地方我们忽略了超级面孔识别的应用？

sentences.en: What are you looking for in your company?
sentences.zh: 你在寻找什么样的人？

sentences.en: Are you expanding?
sentences.zh: 你们在扩张吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, we certainly are.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们当然在扩张。

sentences.en: Well, our passion is to help law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们的热情是协助执法部门。

sentences.en: That's what we would like to do is to be able to go to law enforcement agencies and help them to identify super recognisers within their ranks because there are going to be hundreds of them.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们想做的，能够前往执法部门并帮助他们在自己的队伍中识别出超级面孔识别者，因为他们队伍里会有成百上千这样的人。

sentences.en: And it would be fantastic to think that we could identify them, help train them to know their skill better and for them to be used within those police departments for the better.
sentences.zh: 如果能识别出他们，帮助他们更好地了解自己的技能，并让他们在这些警察部门中发挥更好的作用，那将是一件非常棒的事情。

sentences.en: So that's that's our passion.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们的热情所在。

sentences.en: Super recognisers international would love to get out there and get amongst the law enforcement agencies to help them identify their own.
sentences.zh: 国际超级面孔识别希望走出去，深入执法机构，帮助他们识别出自己队伍中的人才。

sentences.en: That's where we think we'd get the best results for society for.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们认为能为社会带来最佳成果的地方。

sentences.en: Well, I want to thank you both for joining us today.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我要感谢你们俩今天能来。

sentences.en: I think you're both doing extraordinarily important work, and I thank you for it.
sentences.zh: 我认为你们俩都在做着极其重要的工作，我对此表示感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks so much, Kim.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，金。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at www.speakingofpsychology.org or on Apple, Stitcher, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或在苹果、Stitcher 以及你获取播客的任何地方找到往期的《心理学闲谈》节目。

sentences.en: And if you can, please leave us a review.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，请给我们留个评论。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以发电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: That's speakingofpsychology, all one word, at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 也就是 speakingofpsychology，连在一起，@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学闲谈》由李·韦纳曼（Lee Weinerman）制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Condayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的音频剪辑师是克里斯·孔代扬（Chris Condayan）。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills），代表美国心理学会向您问候。
